messages:

Subject: NovaLabs dedicated capacity — post-call summary + asks

Hi Elliot / NovaLabs infra team,

Thanks again for the call earlier — useful to see the live workload. Short recap and concrete asks so we can size a Dedicated pool that meets your latency & streaming needs.

Recap (what you shared):
- Production traffic: ~50 concurrent users for the real-time assistant; peak sessions ~80 during morning ramp.
- Typical session: 120–180 tokens streamed; spike sessions up to ~800 tokens.
- Latency target: 95th <= 120ms for streaming token turn; acceptable up to 200ms during spikes.
- Expected steady-state traffic: ~3k tokens/s; peaks up to 7k tokens/s for 2–3 minutes during batch jobs.

Action items for NovaLabs (please reply to confirm):
1) Confirm whether the 95th latency target is firm at 120ms or flexible to 150ms for the first month of POC.
2) Share a short CSV with representative session token counts (you mentioned you could export last-month-percentiles).
3) Any firm compliance requirements (SLA uptime, region locking) beyond what we discussed?

What we'll deliver next from Redwood:
- A recommended reserved-throughput sizing table (A100 vs H100 cost/latency tradeoff).
- A short perf summary PDF and an editable sizing spreadsheet (attached).
- A proposed POC plan (3-week) with target success criteria.

Attachments: NovaLabs_SizingSpreadsheet_v1.xlsx, redwood_perf-summary-20260820.pdf

Next suggested step: If you can send the CSV, we’ll run an initial throughput model and get back with a suggested reserved throughput and GPU mix by EOD Friday.

Thanks,
Hannah

Elliot / team — dug into the CSV and sketched a short recommendation. High-level:

Findings from CSV (summary):
- Median session small (120–170 tokens) but 99th has long tails to ~900 tokens.
- Burst windows look like 90–180s, peak tokens/s ~6.5k in the sample.

Technical recommendation (tradeoffs):
- GPU choice: H100 gives ~20–35% lower token latency for streaming workloads at small batch sizes due to improved FP16 kernels and NVLink bandwidth; A100 is more cost-efficient for highly batched throughput.
- Quantization: int8 (or int4 for eligible models) reduces memory and can increase effective concurrency; we should validate output quality.
- Reserved throughput: suggest a baseline of 3.5k tokens/s reserved for steady-state, with burst headroom to 8k tokens/s using autoscale + short-duration burst capacity on the same pool.
- Concurrency: size for 80 sustained concurrent streams with a 1.6x headroom for short spikes. That maps roughly to N GPUs depending on model (I sketched 4× H100 or 8× A100 as a starting point for the model and seq lengths you shared).

Operational notes:
- KV cache persistence and prefix caching will help reduce per-token compute for repeated prompts; we should flag the most common prompt prefixes during POC.
- We'll attach a perf summary and a small matrix comparing A100/H100 latency & throughput (see attached perf pdf and spreadsheet).

Next steps (from infra side):
- If NovaLabs confirms 120ms 95th for customer traffic, recommend including at least 50% of the pool on H100 for streaming routes, remainder on A100 to control cost.
- I'll run a short quantization quality pass on a representative prompt set once you confirm the model variant.

Attached: redwood_perf-summary-20260820.pdf, NovaLabs_SizingSpreadsheet_v1.xlsx

—Aditya

Elliot — quick commercial sketch to align expectations:

Reserved tiers (estimate):
- Baseline (3.5k tokens/s reserved): ~4× A100 equivalent or 2× H100 equivalent; monthly commit ~ $X,XXX (exact pricing after model selection).
- Burst plan: short-duration burst pool (adds headroom to ~8k tokens/s) billed on usage; we can cap spend and notify.
- Discount: we can offer a 30% discount on list for annual committed capacity; quarterly billing available for pilot.

Procurement & compliance: we can share SOC2 artifacts; region=us controlled. If procurement needs an NDA or SOW template, tell us who to send to and we'll route the right docs.

Proposed timeline:
1) Confirm model and sign minimal pilot MOU — target by 2026-08-28.
2) POC: 3 weeks, week of 2026-09-06 start.
3) Post-POC: sizing review and committed-reservation proposal.

Can you confirm preferred start week and the primary NovaLabs engineers to include? Also, do you want Redwood to run an initial perf run in our sandbox (fast) or in a NovaLabs-provided VPC (takes longer but closest to prod)?
